answer_summary: One valid PL1 enantiomer is the cardiolipin constitution with identical R residues and R configuration at both peripheral glycerol C2 stereocentres; its mirror is S,S and the mixed assignments are meso. Monoanion Y has one deprotonated phosphate and one protonated phosphate folded around the central glycerol OH, which donates to the anionic phosphate and accepts from the remaining P-OH. The two hydrogen bonds give symmetry-related left- and right-deprotonated canonical forms and make the second deprotonation less favourable.
assumptions: The four problem-authorized R labels denote identical hydrocarbon portions of fatty-acid residues; their internal atoms are intentionally abstracted.
The source calls PL1 a cardiolipin; the standard constitutional definition used is two diacylated peripheral glycerols joined through two phosphate diesters to a central glycerol.
The problem-stated special stabilization of Y is represented by a strictly positive monoanion stabilization free energy.
The thermodynamic explanation uses the standard relation deltaG_standard = R*T*ln(10)*pKa with R*T > 0.
Phosphorus configurations are excluded exactly as directed by the problem.
source_gaps: The problem gives no numerical definition or lower-bound factor for the qualitative symbol pKa2 >> pKa1, so the formal theorem proves the strict ordering pKa2 > pKa1 and does not invent a quantitative gap.
